territorial_scope.description: Applies to Washington State executive and small cabinet agencies; vendors are reached indirectly through required procurement terms.

evidence.quote: all executive and small cabinet agencies as follows

summary.short: Executive Order 24-01 directs executive and small cabinet agencies to govern state use and procurement of generative AI. It sets deadlines from September 2024 to January 2025 for reports, guidelines, risk assessments, vendor governance certification, workforce assessment and training, and research partnerships. Effective on signature, 30 January 2024.
summary.long: The order applies to executive and small cabinet agencies and sets rules for state government use and procurement of generative AI. Section 1 defines generative AI technology and high-risk generative AI systems. Deadlines run from September 2024 to January 2025: a WaTech report on generative AI initiatives and pilot infrastructure (section 2); WaTech and DES guidelines on procurement, use and monitoring, requiring vendors of high-risk systems to certify an AI governance program consistent with the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (section 3); a DES training plan for state workers (section 4); guidelines on impact on vulnerable communities and criteria for high-risk use cases (section 5); updated procurement templates (section 6); an Office of Equity accountability framework (section 7); WaTech risk-assessment guidance (section 8); an assessment of generative AI's impact on the state workforce (section 9). The Workforce Training and Education Coordinating Board is encouraged to form research partnerships by January 2025 (section 10). Agencies act consistent with federal and state law, federal law supersedes inconsistent provisions, and the order creates no enforceable rights (sections 11-12). The order states no penalties.

notes: Text is the order as signed on 30 January 2024; no amended or consolidated version is provided, so no amends or repeals are recorded. Target IDs are blank because none of the referenced instruments is identified in the registry. Internal inconsistencies: 'High-Risk Generative AI System' is defined in paragraph 1(b), but paragraphs 5, 8 and 8(c) use 'AI System' or 'High-Risk AI System', and 'AI System' is undefined. Paragraph 8(g) names the 'National Institute of Science and Technology', while paragraphs 3 and 8 name the 'National Institute of Standards and Technology'. The source spells 'AI' as 'Al' in several places. Paragraph 12 states the order creates no enforceable legal rights.

thresholds.note: The order sets no numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment. Dates in paragraphs 2 to 10 (September 2024, December 2024, January 2025) are procedural deadlines and are coded as events, not thresholds. The definitions of Generative AI Technology and High-Risk Generative AI System in paragraph 1 are qualitative, with no numeric cutoff. Paragraph 3 refers to vendor certification but sets no numeric threshold.
